scope: Exposed conversation development regressions; no held-out or calibrated-judge claim.
fixed: Misleading generated history never enters later source retrieval or prompts.
Former-wife wording and object/possessive pronouns preserve the requested meaning.
Lowercase withheld aliases and performer names never become the wrong character IDs.
An explicit subject cannot invent a missing unnamed object.
Named objects cannot overwrite a preceding retained subject pronoun.
A single clarification choice cannot collapse distinct unnamed participants.
Surname, supported partial-name and demonstrative selections resume the retained user question.
Unknown full names retain clarification even after a matching partial-name choice.
Relationship references create a context barrier so a relative is never inferred to be its named owner.
Reset, context expiry and truncation cannot recover older identities from saved responses.
Concurrent turns retain unique UUIDs and monotonic session turn numbers.
limits: Deterministic English reference rules cover the reviewed cases. They are not unrestricted natural-language coreference resolution.
Use complete reviewed names/aliases in free text. Unique partial names are accepted as bare clarification choices.
Questions with distinct unnamed participants, unsupported relationship/event references or uncertain context require an explicit question with names.
A relationship question can be answered from fresh evidence, but later references require names; generated answers do not supply a relative's identity.
The earlier #7 Janine/context and explicit garage co-ownership gaps remain unchanged under #24/#9.
No live model quality has been accepted for #8 until the budgeted sample is authorized and reviewed.
